title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = -x^(3/2)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = -x^(3/2), state whether it has any symmetry, and specify the intervals where the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.

steps.title: Find the Domain and Check Symmetry
steps.explanation: The fractional exponent 3/2 involves a square root, restricting the natural domain to [0, inf). Because no negative x-values belong to the domain, the graph has no symmetry.
steps.why: Real power functions with even root denominators are defined only on [0, inf).

steps.title: Analyze Monotonicity on [0, inf)
steps.explanation: On [0, inf), x^(3/2) is strictly increasing because both sqrt(x) and u^3 are strictly increasing. Multiplying by -1 reverses the inequality, so -x^(3/2) is strictly decreasing on [0, inf).
steps.why: The negative of a strictly increasing function is strictly decreasing.

steps.title: State the Monotonicity Intervals
steps.explanation: The graph starts at (0, 0) and descends steeply into Quadrant IV through (1, -1) and (4, -8), decreasing over its entire domain [0, inf).
steps.why: As x increases on [0, inf), -x^(3/2) decreases monotonically toward -infinity.
